Hyperscale data centers use 2% of US electricity
raw_text: One flashpoint for the tech industry’s all-in push on large language models has been the sudden rush to turn investment money into hyperscale data centers. The rush hasn’t allowed anyone to plan how to supply the required electricity cleanly or with minimal impact on ratepayers. Instead, it has been difficult to even collect information on what’s being built. A new study has tallied energy use and estimated emissions for hyperscalers operating in the United States between May 2024 and April 2025. They weren’t able to differentiate between AI compute and more traditional data services, but it provides a clear point of reference to track moving forward. Finding the centers The team started with a list of 675 facilities from a commercial database based on news reports, company statements, and satellite imagery. They dropped any that didn’t have a reported electrical capacity or that they couldn’t verify was a suitably large building with the expected cooling and electrical connection equipment. That reduced the list to 403 data centers with an average electrical capacity of about 40 megawatts. Read full article Comments

title: Shareholders sue Intel, its CEO, and CFO after stock drops 28.6 percent in one day
raw_text: Intel is being sued by shareholders, who are accusing the chipmaker of misleading them about the impact of the PC sales slump that contributed to a drop of 28.6 percent in the price of Intel's stock on October 30. The lawsuit ( PDF ), filed on Friday in the San Jose, California, federal court, is seeking class-action certification and lists the City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System and “all others similarly situated” as plaintiffs. In addition to Intel, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan and Intel’s EVP and CFO David Zinsner are listed as defendants. The plaintiffs claim that Intel made “materially false and misleading statements and omissions” between July 23 and October 29. They are seeking unspecified compensatory damages, plus legal and other associated fees, for shareholders during that period. Read full article Comments

title: Comcast's "fiber-powered Wi-Fi" is just cable, AT&T says in false advertising case
raw_text: AT&T on Friday accused Comcast of false advertising in a lawsuit challenging the marketing claim that Comcast's cable broadband service and Wi-Fi is "fiber-powered." "This case challenges Comcast’s false advertising campaign for its residential Internet service, marketed under the Xfinity brand to consumers nationwide," AT&T's lawsuit said. "At the center of that campaign is Comcast’s claim that Xfinity Internet and its associated Wi-Fi service are 'Fiber-Powered.'" While Comcast has deployed plenty of fiber throughout the US, its cable Internet service makes the final connection to homes with coaxial cable. This results in upload speeds being far slower than download speeds. Read full article Comments

title: Supreme Court keeps injunction against DEI grant defunding in place
raw_text: On Monday, the Supreme Court announced it would not hear an appeal of a lower court decision that blocked the government from canceling the grants of a handful of researchers whose funding had been revoked during the Trump administration's purge of DEI-related work. While the decision applies to only seven researchers in California, the lower court had ruled that the government's actions violated the First Amendment and so may have broad implications. The Supreme Court provided no discussion of its rejection, and no justices filed a dissent regarding the decision. The suit was initially filed by a large group of researchers at the University of California, Berkeley and UC San Francisco, contesting grants originally issued by many federal agencies, from the National Institutes of Health to the Department of Transportation. At issue were grants that had been terminated because the agencies decided they violated a Trump executive order blocking the use of DEI. This occurred despite the fact that the government hadn't bothered to define DEI , and targeted grants were often identified by little more than a keyword search . Read full article Comments

title: When will humans actually fly on Starship?
raw_text: The stunning return of Starship from the skies to a launch tower in South Texas answered some questions about the future of SpaceX's ambitious rocket program. Namely, it is now rapidly moving toward rapidly reusable launch. However, it raises other questions. For example, as Starship becomes fully reusable, when might humans fly on the vehicle? The short answer is pretty simple: If SpaceX prioritizes human spaceflight on Starship, it could happen reasonably quickly. The longer answer becomes more complicated and depends on what one means by human spaceflight. The first people to fly on Starship probably won't launch from Earth, or land here. Rather, they will probably be NASA's lunar astronauts. So there are different timelines for humans flying aboard Starship and landing on Earth. Read full article Comments

title: Meet the new James Bond: Robert Pattinson
raw_text: The Internet has been abuzz for months about which actor would replace Daniel Craig as British agent 007 James Bond in the franchise. We finally have the answer: Robert Pattinson , who built on his 2005 role as the doomed Cedric Diggory in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire into an illustrious career mixing roles in franchises and Hollywood blockbusters with daring arthouse fare. “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” Pattinson said in a statement . “To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.” The choice will reunite Pattinson with Denis Villeneuve, who recently worked with him on the forthcoming Dune: Part III and will direct the next (as yet untitled) Bond installment. “I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey," Villeneuve said in a statement . We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.” Read full article Comments

title: US moves to cut China’s remote access to AI chips
raw_text: On the heels of the Nvidia scandal , the Trump administration is preparing to crack down on foreign data centers that are fueling China’s advancements in artificial intelligence by allowing remote access to otherwise restricted high-end chips necessary for AI training. In a summary of the rule change, the Commerce Department said it was closing a loophole that previously allowed foreign rivals like China, Russia, and Iran to bypass export curbs on certain advanced computer chips by instead renting access to those chips from data centers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil. US rivals could possibly use that access to train and run advanced AI models “capable of supporting military- and intelligence-related activities that could threaten US national security or foreign policy interests,” the Commerce Department said. Among threats, the US fears rivals could use advanced AI to develop "more effective weapons of mass destruction and advanced conventional weapons, coordinated cyber-espionage and targeted cyber-disruption, algorithmic theft, and weaponized disinformation.” Read full article Comments

title: US now "comfortable" with children dying of measles as death toll hits 10
raw_text: Health officials in Pennsylvania and Wisconsin announced two more measles deaths late last week, bringing the national tally of confirmed measles deaths this year to 10. The total includes the deaths of at least four infants: two in Pennsylvania , one in New York , and one in Wisconsin . Wisconsin health officials said the latest measles death—the second for the state—was in a child. Pennsylvania's health department did not reveal the age or other details of the latest death—the state's seventh—besides revealing it was of an unvaccinated resident in Montour County. Overall, the seven deaths in Pennsylvania include two in Jefferson County, three in Lancaster County, and one in Mifflin, in addition to the new death in Montour. An eighth death was reported in Franklin County , but state health officials have not confirmed it. For all the states with deaths so far, health officials have noted that they're the first deaths in decades. Multiple outbreaks are underway across the country, pushing the national tally of cases to nearly 5,500 across 47 states and jurisdictions, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Pennsylvania's case count alone is over 1,500, and Wisconsin is reporting nearly 650. Read full article Comments

title: Als verdwijnt wat ons beschermd
raw_text: In Europa staan belangrijke rechten nog steeds onder druk dankzij de verschillende omnibussen. Dat zijn wetsvoorstellen waarmee, via een versneld proces, Europese wetten ‘versimpeld’ moeten worden. Denk daarbij aan wetten die over onze gezondheid, veiligheid en leefomgeving gaan, maar ook over onze privacy. Onze rechten op de onderhandelingstafel Door middel van digitale omnibussen worden belangrijke wetten, waaronder de AI-verordening en de Algemene verordening gegevensbescherming afgezwakt onder het mom van ‘versimpeling van administratieve lasten’. Eerder dit jaar werd er al een knoop doorgehakt over de wijzigingen in de AI-verordening. Net voordat de wet in werking zou treden, werd de wet al gewijzigd en werd de implementatietermijn uitgesteld. Hierdoor treedt de wet die AI in Europa moet reguleren nóg later in werking, terwijl de ontwikkeling daarvan in razend tempo doorgaat. Over wijzigingen die onder andere over de Algemene verordening gegevensbescherming gaan, wordt nog volop onderhandeld. Op 21 oktober heeft de Raad van de Europese Unie namens de Europese lidstaten een positie ingenomen. Nu is het aan het Europees Parlement om een positie in te nemen. Vervolgens zullen de triloog onderhandelingen plaatsvinden tussen de Europese Commissie, de Raad van de Europese Unie en het Europees Parlement. Als verdwijnt wat ons beschermd De afgelopen periode hebben we onze zorgen over de omnibussen gedeeld met de Tweede Kamer, Eerste Kamer, betrokken ministeries en andere partije

title: Show HN: Coral – Open-source gateway where agents write their own tools
raw_text: Hi HN, I'm James, one of the co-founders of Coral. Coral is an open-source, self-hosted gateway that sits between your agents and the systems they work on. Agents call tools by writing short TypeScript programs that they can save as custom tools to reuse. You can publish custom tools for groups of agents, so your team’s library of tools adapts to your unique systems, data and use cases. Custom tools help agent performance and give more precise units of permission control. Here’s a short demo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p0PKOlHLyVI We started on this while building an AI SRE. To investigate an incident, the agent had to connect the dots across an ocean of telemetry data and undocumented relationships across internal and external systems. It took broad permissions, a lot of tokens and it would start from scratch the next time. We built Coral so that the agent remembers the route. Once a task succeeds, the agent writes the steps that worked into a program and saves it as a custom tool. Next time, the agent finds that custom tool in the same search as standard provider tools (e.g. Datadog, Slack), and reuses it. It started with SRE, but we (and our early users) now use Coral for agent work across the org. For our tasks across GitHub, Linear and Slack with Opus 5.5, custom tools help agents work 29% faster, at 31% lower cost (tasks here: https://withcoral.com/docs/examples/custom-tools ). Coral builds on code mode, adding custom tools, policy controls and managed identities.

SAN FRANCISCO—When Ars first drove the new Mercedes-Benz CLA last year , the automaker also gave us a sneak preview of its next driver assist. Called Drive Assist Pro, it’s for collaborative partially assisted driving, and from the passenger seat at the time, the demo was impressive . Now the automaker is getting ready to start rolling out Drive Assist Pro to customers with cars running the new MB.OS operating system here in the US and in Germany, and it let us have some time behind the wheel. While most automakers want a reputation for safety, Mercedes has long used passive and active technology to do so in its products. It was one of the first OEMs to introduce airbags, and a decade later started adding active safety systems like anti-lock brakes, electronic stability control, and adaptive cruise control. And so, by giving the car’s electronics the ability to control the brakes and throttle, we arrive at the first level of assisted driving—called “level 1” in automotive engineer-speak. “Level 2” assisted driving, where the car also controls the steering as well as the acceleration and braking, got famous with Tesla Autopilot. title: Vacature: Beleidsmedewerker privacy en AI
raw_text: We zoeken een beleidsmedewerker privacy en AI. Je kunt tot en met 22 november solliciteren. Kom jij ons team versterken? Please note: proficiency in the Dutch language is a requirement for this position. Over Bits of Freedom Bits of Freedom is een organisatie met grote ambities. We geloven dat een sterke democratische rechtsstaat nodig is om in vrijheid en gelijkheid samen te leven. De macht van technologie moet in handen zijn van de mensen die hier naar streven. In een digitale samenleving zijn het recht op privacy en communicatievrijheid essentieel om de macht van mensen te vergroten en dat van overheden en bedrijven te beknotten. title: UvA-onderzoekers kritisch op EU-voorstel digitale autonomie
raw_text: Het Europese voorstel voor een Cloud and AI Development Act (Cada) is niet ambitieus genoeg om de digitale autonomie van Europa te vergroten. De onderzoekers van het Instituut voor Informatierecht (IViR) van de Universiteit van Amsterdam stellen dat na een analyse van de Cada. Dit voorstel voor een Cada beoogt de Europese cloud- en ai-sector te versterken en de afhankelijkheid van Amerikaanse aanbieders te verkleinen. Volgens de onderzoekers schiet het echter tekort. Bovendien roepen de snelle uitbreiding van datacenters en de beperkte aandacht voor duurzaamheid en maatschappelijke impact bij hun zorgen op. De EU zoekt het in meer aantrekkelijke investeringsvoorwaarden voor grootschalige uitbreiding van datacenters. Tegelijkertijd moeten er regels komen voor de inkoop van clouddiensten door de overheid. Maar de onderzoekers vinden dat de EU daar niet ver genoeg in gaat. Belemmerd Zij tellen dat overheden bij veel diensten beperkt worden in de mogelijkheid om extra eisen te stellen en zo hun afhankelijkheid te verminderen. ‘Zoals het er nu voorstaat, zou dit EU-voorstel overheidsinstellingen zelfs tegenhouden als ze bewust voor een Europees alternatief willen kiezen’, aldus onderzoekster Kristina Irion. Zij vreest dat het streven naar digitale autonomie zelfs door Cada kan worden belemmerd. Deze act koppelt strengere eisen aan clouddiensten aan het risiconiveau van overheidstaken. title: Snowflake brengt bedrijfs- en pro­duct­be­vei­li­ging onder één dak
raw_text: Snowflake heeft de beveiliging van het eigen bedrijf en die van zijn platform onder één verantwoordelijke gebracht. Die rol ligt sinds januari bij Mayank Upadhyay, chief security and trust officer. Hij sprak met Computable tijdens zijn bezoek aan Rotterdam. Upadhyay werkte 21 jaar bij Google, laatst als vp van het beveiligingsplatform van Google Cloud . Naar eigen zeggen leidde zijn team er onder meer werk aan zero trust, tweestapsverificatie, Fido en passkeys. Zijn overstap verklaart hij vanuit de data: modellen komen van overal, maar de data maakt het verschil. Het mandaat omvat volgens Upadhyay een ‘dubbele scope’: Snowflake zelf beveiligen en klanten helpen het platform veilig in te richten en te gebruiken. Die combinatie ontstond na zijn komst. Hij noemt het logisch bij een platformaanbieder. Een probleem op het platform raakt meerdere klanten tegelijk, waardoor beveiliging volgens hem lastig bij een externe leverancier onder te brengen is. Bovendien zou het leveranciersaanbod de specifieke eisen niet altijd bijhouden. Snowflake draait naar eigen zeggen volledig op zijn eigen platform (‘Snow on Snow’). Wat het voor zichzelf ontwikkelt, biedt het daarna aan klanten aan. Guardrails zoals Kimi Antonelli Bij ai-agents ziet Upadhyay nog uitdagingen. Bedrijven moeten volgens hem opgebouwde rechten opschonen, omdat agents bij te ruime toegang kunnen verrassen.
